answer.stillOpen: Nothing for this question. The general point it proved is worth carrying: the first instruction on this record was to check whether the publisher page already in hand prints an amendment note before treating the question as outside research. It did, and the answer took minutes. That instruction is now standard on any provision-dating question.
answer.summary: January 3, 1959, for both sections. The Lieutenant Governor's edition states that the constitution "became operative with the formal Proclamation of Statehood on January 3, 1959". That date governs sections 2 and 3 because their present words are the original ones, and the evidence for that is the publisher's own convention rather than an absence read hopefully: the edition marks an amended section with a bracketed year, and Article II's body carries three such markers - 1984 on section 5 and 1976 twice - while sections 2 and 3 carry none. A convention demonstrably applied to these sections' own neighbors makes its silence here evidence. Recorded at b53f137d; Alaska now opens on an ordinary 2026-01-05 start.

title: When the present words of Alaska Const. art. II, sections 2-3 took effect
usableAnswer: One row: the date the current language of each section took effect, whether that is a ratification date, a statehood date or a later stated effective date, and the material that establishes it. If the sections have never been amended since the constitution took effect, say that explicitly with the source, because that is the answer rather than an absence. If no material establishes it, say so with what you checked; the present refusal is the safe outcome and is much better than a guessed date.
whyItMatters: Alaska's legislator qualifications are refused on an ordinary January 5, 2026 start because the constitution was read on September 6, 2026 and nothing records when its words actually took effect. This is the same defect that kept anyone from standing for office in Nebraska, in a second file. Alaska is one of two states with authored candidacy rules at all, so the refusal removes a large part of what can be played.
